subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Daytona 500
description: A quick win: understand The Daytona 500.

hook.text: NASCAR's biggest race is held on a 2.5-mile superspeedway where cars hit 200 mph in packs.

buildup.text: Daytona's steep 31-degree banking lets cars run flat out without lifting, separated by inches.

discovery.text: Drafting—tucking behind another car to cut air resistance—is so powerful it defines every strategy.

twist.text: The pack racing creates spectacular crashes when one car's wobble triggers a chain reaction at 200 mph.

climax.text: Dale Earnhardt's fatal crash in the 2001 Daytona 500 transformed NASCAR's approach to driver safety.

punchline.text: The Great American Race is both the most watched and most feared.

quiz.question: What racing technique defines strategy at Daytona?

details.summary: The Daytona 500 is NASCAR's most prestigious race, held annually at the Daytona International Speedway, where 43 stock cars battle for 200 laps at speeds exceeding 200 mph on the banked superspeedway.
details.whyItMatters: Known as the Great American Race, the Daytona 500 opens the NASCAR season and attracts millions of viewers. Its pack racing at 200 mph produces spectacular and unpredictable finishes.
takeaways: It has been held annually at Daytona since 1959
Cars reach over 200 mph on the 2.5-mile tri-oval
Restrictor plates limit engine power to keep speeds manageable

faq.question: Why is the Daytona 500 called the Great American Race?
faq.answer: Its combination of prestige, history, massive attendance, and dramatic finishes make it NASCAR's equivalent of the Super Bowl. It is the most-watched race in American motorsport and opens the championship season.

faq.question: What are restrictor plates and why are they used?
faq.answer: Restrictor plates limit airflow to the engine to reduce horsepower and top speed. They were introduced at Daytona and Talladega after Bobby Allison's car nearly flew into the grandstands at over 210 mph in 1987.
